title: Sample Aha — quote process & price objection
description: Short, fictional English B2B sales call for the 'Show me what it does' demo. Contains a pain point (quote process), an objection (price/timing) and coaching moments. No real PII.

events.speaker: self
events.text: Good afternoon, and thanks for taking the call. We help sales teams automate their quotes.

events.speaker: self
events.text: It started with our own team: every Friday our sellers were stitching quotes together from old documents, copying and pasting.

events.speaker: self
events.text: So we built a platform that brings your price list, your terms and your customer data together in one place.

events.speaker: self
events.text: You pick the products, the system works out the discounts, and the quote is ready in your own branding.

events.speaker: self
events.text: It also connects to your CRM, so every change to a deal ends up in the proposal automatically.

events.speaker: self
events.text: Customers can view the quote online, leave comments on it and approve it with a single click.

events.speaker: self
events.text: You can see exactly when someone opens the quote, which sections they read and where they drop off.

events.speaker: self
events.text: Teams that use it send their proposals out three times faster on average, and they lose fewer deals to slow follow-up.

events.speaker: self
events.text: And the rollout is simple: we import your existing templates, train your team in an afternoon and you can start right away. Do you have a few minutes?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Sure, but keep it short. Creating quotes takes us too much time, and that is a real problem for us.

events.speaker: self
events.text: That sounds familiar. How does the quote process work for you today?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: We still build every quote manually in Word. Clients wait too long for a quote, sometimes several days.

events.speaker: self
events.text: And if you could cut that time in half, what would that mean for the team?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: That would be great, but this is too expensive for us. We do not have budget for this right now.

events.speaker: self
events.text: I understand. What if the investment paid for itself within a quarter?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: My manager still needs to review this. We want to pick this up next quarter.

events.speaker: self
events.text: No problem. Can I schedule a short follow-up call with you and your manager?

events.speaker: prospect
events.text: Yes, please do. Send a short proposal to our general mailbox and we will get back to you.

questions: How many hours a week does the quote process cost you right now?
Who exactly builds the quotes today?
What happens when a quote goes out a day late?
What do you mean by 'too expensive': the monthly cost or the setup?
How do you decide the budget for this kind of tooling?
What would it be worth to you to have quotes ready within a day?
When would your manager have time for this?
What matters most to your manager?
Can I send a business case you can forward?
